articles.headline: Cole Palmer's England withdrawal a product of 'sick' system - PFA chief
articles.description: Cole Palmer's recent England withdrawal is the product of a "sick" system that is demanding too much of the game's stars, according to Professional Footballers' Association chief executive Maheta Molango.
articles.body:
Cole Palmer's recent England withdrawal is the product of a "sick" system that is demanding too much of the game's stars, according to Professional Footballers' Association chief executive Maheta Molango.

Palmer is one of five injured players to pull out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for the current round of Nations League fixtures in a trend that Molango says is mirrored across the Europe because of an unsustainable workload.

The PFA boss wants FIFA to look again at what is being asked of players, insisting they are paying the price for the expansion of the World Cup and the Club World Cup for reasons "which have nothing to do with the good of the game."

"When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what's wrong about the industry?" Molango said at the FIFPRO performance summit in London.

"You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?

"He's missing because he's a victim of the calendar and that's something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.

"For those who think that it's only a matter in England, then look at [other recent withdrawals from European teams] Kai Havertz, Brian Brobbey and Kylian Mbappé and ask yourself -- is that really the football that we want?

"Is it the football where the people who make us dream just cannot perform? For me it's very worrying.

- Anthony Gordon: People respect my football IQ more now I'm at Barcelona

- Why are England playing four games in 11 days? Extended international break explained

- 'England were the biggest dangers to ourselves' against Spain - Thomas Tuchel

"What we've seen over the last few years is a system that's sick, that's ill, because it ultimately revolves around obtaining votes and power consolidation.

"It's a defeat for football that people like Cole Palmer and Phil Foden miss out on the World Cup. They're the people that you pay to see. People don't pay for the journeyman Maheta Molango. People pay to see those type of guys.

"I want to see them perform at their peak and it shouldn't be the survival of the fittest. Unfortunately, both on the male and female sides, that's not what we're seeing."

Apart from an overhaul of the calendar, Molango is calling for players to be given a three-week holiday followed by three weeks of "retraining" every summer.

Premier League chief football officer Rebecca Caplehorn insists that proposal is not viable, however.

"It's something we're really supportive of, conceptually, but the challenge is that it just doesn't fit into the current calendar," Caplehorn said.

"There's always something that's preventing us having that six-week gap that we want. Without regulatory change and change to the calendar, it's not possible for us to deliver that."

articles.headline: NBA preseason: Answering big questions for all 30 teams
articles.description: From LeBron James' fit in Philadelphia to Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto, we're answering the biggest preseason questions for all 30 teams.
articles.body:
Monday's media day kicked off NBA training camps around the league and offered a first look at several stars in their new homes. The Philadelphia 76ers had perhaps the biggest offseason, adding Jaylen Brown on July 1 and then the league's all-time leading scorer LeBron James before the month was over. But the Sixers aren't the only ones who made big moves.

James' former team, the Los Angeles Lakers, took a big swing in trading for former Jazz center Walker Kessler, and Giannis Antetokounmpo finally found a new home in the Miami Heat. LaMelo Ball is teaming up with Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves, and Ja Morant will look for a fresh start with the Portland Trail Blazers.

Big trades and signings aren't the only noteworthy storylines coming out of the offseason. Will the Detroit Pistons resolve Jalen Duren's contract dispute? How will the San Antonio Spurs rebound after collapsing in the Finals? Our NBA Insiders answer the biggest preseason questions for all 30 teams.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

Will the Hawks build on their strong finish to last season?

To be clear, the Hawks' 51-point loss in their elimination game isn't the strong finish we are referring to. But Atlanta did account for two of the Knicks' three playoff losses, and the Hawks went on a 19-4 run with a plus-13.9 average point differential at the end of the regular season after committing to CJ McCollum in the starting lineup.

Atlanta added to the roster this summer -- drafting Kingston Flemings in the lottery and trading for ring-earning role players Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins -- and is positioned to be aggressive at the trade deadline or next summer, when the Hawks could have about $45 million in salary cap space. -- Tim MacMahon

Boston Celtics

Is Jayson Tatum ready to assume command of the Celtics on the court?

Tatum made it a point to get back on the court before last season ended, proving his Achilles injury couldn't keep him down. The results were mixed in the short term, as his regular-season percentages were down across the board and he sat out Game 7 of the Celtics' first-round series because of left knee discomfort.

Trading Jaylen Brown was a full endorsement of Tatum's ability to take the throttle while retooling to get back to championship status. But is Tatum fully recovered from the injury and ready to assume control? -- Vincent Goodwill

Brooklyn Nets

Can the Nets go from deplorable to dependable?

The Nets invested in a long-term rebuilding plan: think of those first-round picks Sean Marks held onto in the 2025 draft, rather than attempting to aggregate them for impact players. But then lottery reform happened, forcing the Nets to press the fast-forward button in July.

Trading for Julius Randle upgraded their talent, as did drafting another point guard in Mikel Brown Jr.

articles.headline: Sources: Panthers OL Damien Lewis (UCL injury) to miss time
articles.description: Panthers left guard Damien Lewis has a UCL injury in his elbow and will be out a few weeks, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers starting left guard Damien Lewis will be sidelined a few weeks with a UCL injury in his elbow, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport on Tuesday.

A source classified Lewis' UCL injury as a tear to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Medical evaluations of Lewis' injury are ongoing.

Lewis will at least miss the Panthers' game Sunday night against the Detroit Lions.

The Panthers have a bye in Week 5 so there's a chance he might miss only one game.

Lewis was injured in the first half of Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns, but he returned in the third quarter to finish out the game.

Lewis has been one of the Panthers' highest performing offensive linemen through three games, while left tackle Rasheed Walker, a free agent who was signed to a one-year deal in March, has had a challenging time in his three games played. Rookie Monroe Freeling has been manning the right-hand side.

The Panthers are dealing with several injuries, as top cornerback Jaycee Horn is out indefinitely after suffering a torn quad in Week 3's loss to the Browns. Longtime starting tackles Taylor Moton (blood clot) and Ikem Ekwonu (patellar tendon) are eligible to return from the non-football injury list and physically unable to perform list, respectively, following the bye.

ESPN's Mike Kaye contributed to this report.

articles.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
articles.description: The NBA regular season is less than a month away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Goodwill on the latest between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns: "It wasn't so much what he said, like this full-throated defense of himself, but he said, 'I would like to get my contract done.'

"He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up.

"And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'"
